thread:
oncall-bot: [PAGER] INCIDENT ALERT: DeltaCorp (dedicated-pool-12) - redaction pipeline exception detected. Possible unredacted PII in forwarded logs. Pager: @ashley. Please acknowledge.

ashley: acked. pulling context now. which pipeline threw the exception? any sample lines?

oncall-bot: redaction-service-2 reported: "redact_fail: RuleMismatchError" on 2026-03-15T14:12:03Z. Last forwarded batch to: s3://delta-logs/raw/2026/03/15/14/

kevin: I'm on network infra. Ashley, can you confirm whether this is only metadata or full request bodies? DeltaCorp has stricter retention - need to know scope asap.

ashley: grabbing a sample from the dead-letter queue. list of redaction rules shows an unexpected rule drop for the tenant. sample (sanitized for channel):

```
2026-03-15T14:11:58Z | tenant=delta-corp | request_id=abc123 | user_id=delta_user_98765 | text="Customer SSN: 123-45-6789" | route=ingest-raw
```

ashley: that looks like raw PII (SSN) made it into the dead-letter batch that was forwarded to their S3. Not yet public, but stored in our customer-managed bucket.

sanjay: Can we confirm whether the write actually succeeded to the bucket or only staged? ops-bot, any S3 write confirmations?

ops-bot: s3-writer: write_success for key s3://delta-logs/raw/2026/03/15/14/batch-7.json (size 2.1MB) at 2026-03-15T14:12:05Z.

ashley: confirmed. We need to stop further forwarding and prevent searches/retention jobs from touching that path. Immediate mitigations: 1) Disable the redaction forwarder for tenant  delta-corp 2) Quarantine bucket prefix 3) Snapshot for forensics 4) Notify legal and customer ops.

kevin: patching pipeline ACL now. running:

```
# disable forwarder for tenant
kubectl -n logging patch deploy/redaction-forwarder --type=json -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/-","value":{"name":"DISABLE_FORWARD_DELTA","value":"true"}}]'
```

kevin: done. Forwarder config shows DISABLE_FORWARD_DELTA=true. Should prevent new writes but existing objects persist.

maria_legal: maria_legal here. Thx for the ping. DeltaCorp is enterprise with contractual PII handling obligations. We need an incident timeline, exact object keys, and a recommendation for retention/removal. Important: we cannot delete customer data without explicit authorization from the customer and legal approval for our side-effects.

ashley: understood. For timeline: redaction exception started 14:11:58Z. several batches shipped between 14:12:00Z and 14:12:30Z. ops-bot indicates 3 write_success events for keys:
- s3://delta-logs/raw/2026/03/15/14/batch-5.json
- s3://delta-logs/raw/2026/03/15/14/batch-6.json
- s3://delta-logs/raw/2026/03/15/14/batch-7.json

ashley: recommended immediate steps (low-blast first):
- Quarantine prefix by applying bucket policy to deny reads to non-Delta roles (kevin).
- Snapshot current objects to an immutable forensic bucket (for legal).
- Prevent retention jobs / lifecycle transitions on that prefix.
- Prepare customer-facing notification draft and ask delta-eng for approval before any removal.

kevin: applied temporary bucket policy to block anonymous/public and non-deltacorp service roles. Policy id: tmp-quarantine-1778501123. Also created snapshot copy to s3://forensics/delta/1778501123/ (immutable with object lock). Copy status: queued.

customer-eng-delta: @ashley @maria_legal DeltaCorp security here. Thank you for the quick detection. We request immediate redaction and removal of PII from your side, per section 5.3 of the contract. Please advise ETA and action plan.

maria_legal: DeltaCorp's contract requires us to get their written approval for any deletion/remediation that affects their records. We can propose an emergency remediation agreement (email/portal approval). Meanwhile, we must preserve chain-of-custody for forensic copies. I'll draft the emergency remit and ping DeltaCorp legal.

ashley: operational plan while we wait for cust approval:
1) Quarantine (done).
2) Snapshot (in progress).
3) Build and run redaction pass that masks PII in copies: sed/perl-based scrub, then produce sanitized copies to s3://delta-logs/sanitized/2026/03/15/14/ (for internal debugging).
4) Audit logs for any external access to those objects.

kevin: started scrub job on a duplicate copy (not touching original objects). scrub command (running in k8s pod):

```
python scripts/scrub_pii.py --input s3://forensics/delta/1778501123/ --output s3://delta-logs/sanitized/2026/03/15/14/ --rules config/redaction-rules.yaml --tenant delta-corp
```

kevin: job logs show matches for SSN and credit_card tokens; scrub produced sanitized files. Hashes for forensic originals preserved in metadata.

maria_legal: Good. Keep chain-of-custody and hashes. Do NOT delete originals until we have customer instruction. Also need to prepare a minimal customer notice that doesn't over-disclose internal details. I'll prepare language.

ashley: raising an internal RCA ticket: INC-DELTA-1778501123. Root cause appears to be a rule indexing bug in redaction-service-2 where tenant-specific rule overrides were skipped under load. triage assigned to eng-ml and eng-runtime.

sanjay: assigning to eng-runtime for immediate patch and to eng-ml for rule validation. Also flagging for a postmortem and a policy update for retention exceptions.

oncall-bot: Reminder: next on-call handover in 20min. Ashley, are you handing off?

ashley: I'll be on for next 30m then hand to kevin for overnight monitoring. kevin, please accept on-call for DeltaCorp escalation.

kevin: accepted. I'll monitor scrub progress and S3 access logs. If customer approves deletion, coordinate with maria_legal for documented approval and run delete with audit trail.

maria_legal: DeltaCorp legal responded: they confirm they want PII removed from our copies and will provide written authorization for us to purge the objects we originated. They also request a forensic bundle (hashes + timeline) be delivered. DeltaCorp requested this within 6 hours. I'll post the signed approval in private thread and escalate if needed.

ashley: once signed approval is in hand: 1) we'll mark originals for deletion in a controlled job that records initiator, timestamp, and object hashes 2) we'll run a final scrub pass to ensure no PII in sanitized outputs 3) we'll update incident ticket with timelines and send the forensic bundle.

kevin: noted. I'll prepare the deletion job to be run only after an explicit trigger:

```
# deletion, only after legal trigger
aws s3 rm s3://delta-logs/raw/2026/03/15/14/ --recursive --include "batch-*.json" --dryrun
# after approval, run without --dryrun and record output to secure log
```

kevin: also adding a safeguard: require two approvers (maria_legal + delta-signed) to flip the feature flag REMOVE_ARRIVED_PII.

customer-eng-delta: we have the signed emergency approval, attaching in DM. Please proceed with removal and share forensic bundle when done.

maria_legal: received signed approval. Proceed with deletion per SLA and preserve forensic bundle copies. Legal will coordinate any customer communications and regulatory notifications if needed.

ashley: initiating controlled delete now. running with kevin supervision. will post results.

ops-bot: delete_job: completed. Removed 3 objects from s3://delta-logs/raw/2026/03/15/14/ (batch-5.json, batch-6.json, batch-7.json). Audit log: s3-audit://audit/1778501123/delete.log (access restricted).

kevin: deletion confirmed and logged. Forensic bundle prepared at s3://forensics/delta/1778501123/bundle.tar.gz with SHA256 checksum: abcdef123456... (maria_legal has copy).

maria_legal: will draft final customer-facing summary and internal postmortem requirements. Also opening a policy ticket to require tenant-specific unit tests for redaction rules on rollout.

ashley: handing incident to kevin for overnight watch. I'll update INC-DELTA-1778501123 with final notes and close once postmortem is scheduled. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

kevin: ack. Monitoring for 2 hours then hand to next rotation. Closing Slack thread for now, will reopen if anything new shows up.

oncall-bot: Incident marked: PII exposure (contained). Status: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident owner: kevin.
